value.rationale: The reset-multiplier law is an experimentally meaningful design degree of freedom for intermittently returning diffusers, yet fixing stationary variance leaves large changes in non-Gaussian shape. The theorem yields a complete, attained all-protocol clock convex-order interval and sharp kurtosis interval with unique endpoint protocols, plus a counterintuitive peakedness/absolute-displacement tradeoff.
